title: Mexican-Style Crispy Potato and Pinto Bean Tacos (Tacos de Papa)
description: Corn tortillas folded around a cumin-spiced potato and pinto bean mash, pan-fried until crisp, and topped with lime cabbage and salsa. Twelve tacos for four people at about $1.40 a serving.
notes: The filling should be thick enough to hold a spoon upright; if it is loose, cook it a few minutes longer in the skillet so the tacos do not leak while frying. Cold tortillas crack when folded, so warm them right before filling and keep them covered. Crumbled cotija or queso fresco on top is traditional but adds milk and makes the tacos no longer vegan. The filling keeps in the refrigerator for 4 days and freezes for 2 months, so you can fry a few tacos at a time; fried tacos are best right away but reheat on a dry skillet or in a 400°F oven for 8 minutes. Check the tortilla package if you need them certified gluten-free. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat the filling to 165°F.

ingredients.name: yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
pinto beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
tomato salsa or pico de gallo

instructions: Put the potatoes in a medium pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, and add 1 teaspoon of the salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until a knife slides through the largest piece with no resistance. Drain well.

While the potatoes cook, heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring, for about 5 minutes, until soft and translucent. Stir in the garlic, cumin, and chili powder and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Add the pinto beans and the 2 tablespoons water and mash roughly with a potato masher. Add the drained potatoes and the remaining 1 teaspoon salt and mash until mostly smooth with a few small lumps. Taste and adjust the salt, then scrape the filling into a bowl and wipe out the skillet.
Toss the cabbage with the lime juice and a pinch of salt and set it aside to soften slightly while you assemble the tacos.

Wrap the tortillas in a damp kitchen towel and microwave for 45 to 60 seconds, until hot and pliable. Working with a few at a time, spread a scant 1/4 cup of filling over half of each tortilla, fold it closed, and press gently to seal.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Fry 4 tacos at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side, pressing lightly with a spatula, until golden and crisp. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate and add more oil between batches as needed.
Open each taco slightly and tuck in some lime cabbage and a spoonful of salsa. Top with cilantro and jalapeño if you like, and serve hot.

title: Pasta e Piselli: Italian-Style Ditalini with Peas and Parmesan
description: A Neapolitan-style pot of small pasta cooked right in a brothy pea and onion base, then finished with Parmesan and black pepper. One pot, pantry staples, and about $1.25 a serving.
equipment: 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven or heavy pot
kettle or small saucepan for hot water
notes: The finished pot should be loose and spoonable, somewhere between a thick soup and a saucy pasta; the pasta keeps drinking liquid as it sits, so serve it right away. Traditional Parmesan is made with animal rennet, so strict vegetarians should look for a rennet-free hard cheese. For a dairy-free and vegan version, skip the cheese and stir in 3 tablespoons nutritional yeast with an extra drizzle of olive oil, which removes the milk allergen. Gluten-free short pasta works but cooks faster, so start checking it 2 minutes early. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours for up to 4 days; reheat in a pot with a splash of water or broth, stirring, until steaming hot (165°F). This does not freeze well because the pasta turns soft.

ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
frozen peas (about 3 1/2 cups), no need to thaw
water, hot, plus more as needed
kosher salt, plus more to taste
parmesan cheese, finely grated (about 1 cup, 57 g)
freshly ground black pepper, plus more for serving

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and a pinch of the salt and cook, stirring often, for 7 to 8 minutes, until soft and pale gold but not browned.
Stir in the garlic and the red pepper flakes, if using, and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato paste and cook, stirring, for 1 minute more, until it darkens slightly and coats the onion.

Add the frozen peas, broth, hot water, and the remaining salt. Raise the heat to high and bring to a boil, then crush about a quarter of the peas against the side of the pot with the back of a spoon to help thicken the broth.

Stir in the ditalini and cook at a lively simmer, stirring every minute or so to keep the pasta from sticking, for 10 to 12 minutes, until the pasta is al dente. Whenever the pot looks thick, add more hot water 1/2 cup at a time; the result should be creamy and loose.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in half the Parmesan and the black pepper until the cheese melts into the liquid. Let it rest for 2 minutes, then taste for salt.
Ladle into shallow bowls and top with the remaining Parmesan, a drizzle of olive oil, more black pepper, and the parsley and lemon zest if using. Serve immediately.

title: Chinese-Style Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry (Fanqie Chao Dan) over Rice
description: Soft-scrambled eggs folded into a glossy, sweet-sour sauce of tomatoes cooked down until juicy, spooned over jasmine rice. A home-cooking classic, ready in 35 minutes for about $1.45 a serving.
notes: The ripest tomatoes give the most juice and flavor; out of season, use 1 can (28 oz) whole peeled tomatoes, drained and broken into pieces, plus 1/2 cup of their juice. Pull the eggs while they still look a little wet, because they finish cooking when they go back into the sauce. Many home cooks add 1 teaspoon soy sauce with the ketchup, which adds soy and wheat; most ketchup is gluten-free, but check the label if that matters to you. This is best eaten right away, but leftovers keep for 2 days in the refrigerator. Refrigerate leftovers, including the rice, within 2 hours, and reheat until steaming hot (165°F).

ingredients.name: kosher salt, divided, plus a pinch for the rice
scallions, whites and greens sliced separately
ripe mixed tomatoes (about 5 medium or 7 plum), cut into wedges

instructions: Rinse the rice in a strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Combine it with the 2 1/4 cups water and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan, bring to a boil, then cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it steam, covered, for 10 minutes.

Crack the eggs into a bowl, add 1/2 teaspoon of the salt, and whisk for about 30 seconds, until no streaks of white remain and the eggs look slightly foamy. In a small bowl, stir together the ketchup, sugar, cornstarch, and 1/4 cup water.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Pour in the eggs, let them set for 5 seconds, then push them gently across the pan into large, soft curds, 45 to 60 seconds. Slide them onto a plate while they still look a little wet.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil to the skillet with the scallion whites and garlic and stir for 30 seconds. Add the tomatoes and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and cook, stirring and pressing a few wedges with the spatula, for 4 to 6 minutes, until the tomatoes slump and release plenty of juice but some pieces still hold their shape.
Stir the ketchup mixture, pour it into the skillet, and simmer for about 1 minute, until the sauce turns glossy and lightly thickened.

Return the eggs to the pan and fold gently for 30 seconds, just until heated through and fully set. Taste and add a pinch more sugar if the tomatoes are sharp. Scatter the scallion greens and a few grinds of pepper over the top and serve over the rice.

title: Aloo Matar: North Indian-Style Potato and Pea Curry with Basmati Rice
description: Tender potatoes and sweet peas simmered in a gingery onion-tomato gravy with cumin and garam masala, served over basmati rice. Vegan, gluten-free, and about $1.30 a serving.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven with lid
notes: Cook the onion until it is truly golden and the tomato until the oil pools at the edges; that is where the gravy gets its depth. For less heat, seed the chile and cut the cayenne to a pinch, or use paprika instead. Cubes of paneer added with the peas are a common variation and add milk. The curry keeps for 4 days in the refrigerator and freezes for up to 2 months, though thawed potatoes turn a little soft; add a splash of water when reheating because the gravy thickens as it sits. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot (165°F).

ingredients.name: serrano or green chile, finely chopped
russet or yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
kosher salt, plus a pinch for the rice

instructions: Combine the rinsed rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it steam, covered, while you make the curry.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for about 30 seconds, until they darken a shade and smell toasty.

Add the onion and cook, stirring often, for 8 to 10 minutes, until deep golden. Add the garlic, ginger, and chile and cook for 1 minute, then stir in the turmeric, coriander, and cayenne for 30 seconds.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and cook, stirring and scraping the bottom, for 5 to 6 minutes, until the mixture thickens into a paste and oil starts to separate at the edges.
Add the potatoes, 2 cups water, and the salt and stir well. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer over medium-low heat for 15 to 18 minutes, until a potato cube breaks easily when pressed with a spoon.

Mash a few potato cubes against the side of the pot to thicken the gravy. Stir in the peas and simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes, until the peas are hot and the gravy coats a spoon. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the garam masala, taste for salt, and scatter cilantro over the top. Fluff the rice with a fork and serve the curry over it with lime wedges on the side.

title: Ethiopian-Inspired Gomen (Garlicky Collard Greens) with Brown Lentils and Rice
description: Collard greens braised soft with onion, ginger, garlic, and green chile in the Ethiopian gomen style, served with turmeric-simmered lentils over rice. A big pile of greens and plant protein for about $1.35 a serving.
equipment: 5-quart Dutch oven or heavy pot with lid
notes: Collards need the full braise to turn silky; if they still squeak against your teeth, cover the pot and give them another 5 to 10 minutes with a splash of water. Gomen is often cooked with niter kibbeh, an Ethiopian spiced clarified butter; using 2 tablespoons ghee or butter in place of some of the oil adds milk and makes the dish no longer vegan. Kale works in place of collards and cooks in about 12 minutes. Serve with injera instead of rice if you can find it. The greens and lentils each keep for 4 days in the refrigerator and freeze for up to 3 months. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot (165°F).

ingredients.name: brown or green lentils (200 g), picked over and rinsed
jalapeño, seeded and cut into thin strips

instructions: Combine the lentils, 4 cups water, and turmeric in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 20 to 25 minutes, until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Stir in 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and drain off all but a few spoonfuls of the liquid.

Meanwhile, combine the rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt in a second saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes, then let it steam off the heat, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wash the collards in a sink of cold water and lift them out, leaving any grit behind. Cut out the thick stems, stack the leaves, roll them up, and slice them into 1/2-inch ribbons.

Heat the oil in a 5-quart Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring, for about 8 minutes, until soft and light golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, then stir in the cardamom for 15 seconds.

Add the collards a few handfuls at a time with the water still clinging to them, stirring until each batch wilts. Add the 1/2 cup water and the remaining 1 teaspoon salt, cover, and cook over medium-low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the greens are tender and silky. Add a splash of water if the pot runs dry.
Uncover, add the jalapeño strips, and cook for about 5 minutes more, until most of the liquid has cooked off. Stir in the lemon juice and several grinds of black pepper, and taste for salt.
Spoon the rice into bowls and serve the lentils and gomen side by side over it, with a little of the lentil liquid spooned on top.

title: Greek-Style Briam: Oven-Braised Potatoes, Zucchini and Eggplant in Tomato
description: Potatoes, zucchini, eggplant, and onion baked slowly in olive oil and tomato until soft, sweet, and browned at the edges. Thrifty Greek home cooking, about $1.45 a serving.
notes: Briam is meant to be very soft, with jammy tomato clinging to every piece; if the potatoes are tender but the sauce is still thin, give it another 10 to 15 minutes uncovered. Slice the potatoes thinner than the other vegetables so everything finishes at the same time. Crumbled feta over the top is a classic addition but adds milk and makes it no longer vegan. It tastes even better the next day, warm or at room temperature, with a piece of crusty bread (which adds wheat). Refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 4 days; reheat in a 350°F oven for about 20 minutes or in the microwave until steaming hot (165°F). Freezing is not recommended because the zucchini turns watery.

ingredients.name: yukon gold potatoes, scrubbed and sliced 1/4 inch thick
medium zucchini (about 1 lb), sliced 1/2 inch thick
medium eggplant (about 1 lb), cut into 1-inch chunks
large yellow onion, halved and thinly sliced
extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the center.

In a large bowl, combine the potatoes, zucchini, eggplant, onion, and garlic. Add the crushed tomatoes, olive oil, oregano, salt, pepper, and half the parsley and toss with your hands until every piece is coated.
Spread the vegetables in a 9x13-inch baking dish, packing them in snugly with the potato slices tucked down into the sauce. Pour the water around the edges and cover the dish tightly with foil.
Bake, covered, for 45 minutes, until the potatoes are just tender when pierced with a knife.

Uncover, gently turn the vegetables with a spatula, and bake for 35 to 45 minutes more, until the liquid has cooked down to a thick, jammy sauce, the edges are browned, and the potatoes are completely tender. If the pan looks dry before then, add a splash of water.
Let the briam rest for 15 minutes. Scatter the remaining parsley and the dill over the top, drizzle with a little more olive oil, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Brazilian-Style Feijão with Garlic Rice and Quick Collard Greens (Couve)
description: Dried black beans simmered until creamy with bay leaf and garlic, alongside fluffy garlic rice and thin ribbons of collards sautéed for two minutes. A Brazilian everyday plate for about $1.10 a serving.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
notes: Start soaking the beans the night before; older beans can take up to 2 hours to soften, so taste several before you season. In a pressure cooker, cook the soaked beans with the water and bay leaves for 25 minutes at high pressure with a natural release, then continue with the onion and garlic step. Brazilian cooks often add bacon or smoked sausage to the pot, which makes it no longer vegetarian; smoked paprika gives a similar smoky note here. Orange slices on the side are traditional and cut the richness. The beans keep for 5 days in the refrigerator and freeze in their liquid for 3 months; the rice keeps 4 days. Cool and refrigerate everything within 2 hours, and reheat until steaming hot (165°F).

ingredients.name: dried black beans (454 g), soaked overnight
water, for the beans, plus more as needed
yellow onions, finely chopped, divided (1 large, 1 small)
louisiana-style cayenne pepper hot sauce, for serving

instructions: The night before, put the beans in a large bowl and cover with cold water by 3 inches. The next day, drain and rinse them.

Combine the beans, 8 cups water, and bay leaves in a large heavy pot. Bring to a boil over high heat and skim off any foam, then reduce the heat and simmer, partly covered, for 60 to 90 minutes, until the beans are completely creamy inside. Add hot water as needed to keep them covered.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the large onion and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until golden. Add 4 cloves of the garlic, the smoked paprika, and the cumin and cook for 1 minute.

Scoop about 1 cup of beans with some of their liquid into the skillet and mash them into a rough paste. Scrape it all back into the pot with 1 1/2 teaspoons of the salt and simmer, uncovered, for 15 to 20 minutes, until the broth thickens into a light gravy. Remove the bay leaves, add pepper, and taste for salt.

While the beans finish, heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook the small onion for 3 minutes, add 2 cloves of the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the rice and stir for 2 minutes, until the grains look chalky. Add the boiling water and 3/4 teaspoon of the salt, bring back to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes. Let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Stack the collard leaves, roll them tightly into a cigar, and slice crosswise into very thin ribbons, about 1/8 inch wide.

Just before serving, wipe out the skillet and heat the remaining 1 tablespoon oil over medium-high heat. Add the remaining 2 cloves garlic for 20 seconds, then the collards and the last 1/4 teaspoon salt, and toss for 1 to 2 minutes, until bright green and just wilted.
Serve the rice with the beans ladled alongside, the collards on the side, and lime wedges and hot sauce at the table.

title: Polish-Style Potato and Cheese Pierogi Casserole with Caramelized Onions
description: The flavor of potato and cheese pierogi without pinching a single dumpling: a soft sour cream dough layered with cheddar mashed potatoes and buttery onions, then baked. About $1.20 a serving.
notes: Farmer's cheese (twaróg) is the traditional pierogi cheese; use 1 1/2 cups crumbled in place of the cheddar if you can find it, and the allergens stay the same. Russets make the fluffiest filling and Yukon Golds the creamiest. Keep the dough covered while you roll, and if it springs back, let it rest 10 more minutes. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours for up to 4 days; reheat squares in a 350°F oven for about 15 minutes or in a covered skillet until they reach 165°F. Baked squares freeze for up to 2 months; reheat from frozen at 350°F for about 30 minutes.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour (315 g), plus more for rolling
kosher salt, divided, plus more for the potato water
full-fat sour cream, for the dough
russet or yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 2-inch chunks

instructions: Whisk the flour and 1 teaspoon of the salt in a large bowl. Add the 1/2 cup sour cream, warm water, and oil and stir with a fork until shaggy, then knead in the bowl for 3 to 4 minutes, until smooth and soft. If dry crumbs remain, add water 1 tablespoon at a time. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, and salt the water generously. Bring to a boil and simmer for 15 to 18 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain well and return to the pot off the heat for 2 minutes to steam dry.

While the potatoes cook, melt 2 tablespoons of the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt and cook, stirring often, for 20 to 25 minutes, until soft and deep golden brown. Add a splash of water if they start to stick.
Mash the potatoes with 1 tablespoon of the butter, the cheddar, the remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, the pepper, and half of the onions until smooth. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with a little of the remaining butter. Divide the dough in half and roll each piece on a floured counter into a rectangle about 10 by 14 inches and 1/8 inch thick.

Lay one sheet of dough in the dish, letting it come slightly up the sides. Spread the potato filling over it in an even layer, then cover with the second sheet and tuck the edges down. Melt the last of the butter, brush it over the top, and prick the dough all over with a fork.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the top is golden and blistered. Let rest for 10 minutes, then cut into 12 squares and serve topped with the remaining onions, sour cream, and scallions.

title: Vietnamese-Style Tofu in Tomato Sauce (Đậu Sốt Cà Chua) with Jasmine Rice
description: Golden pan-fried tofu simmered in a quick, savory-sweet tomato and scallion sauce and served over jasmine rice. A Vietnamese family-table staple that comes in at about $1.45 a serving.
notes: Patting the tofu very dry and leaving it alone in the pan is what gives it a golden crust that holds up in the sauce. Many Vietnamese cooks season this with fish sauce; using 1 tablespoon in place of half the soy sauce adds fish and makes the dish no longer vegan. Use gluten-free tamari instead of soy sauce for a gluten-free version, which removes wheat but keeps soy. Out of season, a 14.5 oz can of diced tomatoes with its juice works in place of fresh. Leftovers keep for 3 days in the refrigerator; freezing makes the tofu spongy. Refrigerate leftovers, including the rice, within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot (165°F).

ingredients.name: scallions, whites and greens sliced separately

instructions: Combine the rinsed rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and a pinch of the salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes, then let it steam off the heat, covered, for 10 minutes.

Cut the tofu into 1-inch cubes, spread them on a clean kitchen towel, cover with a second towel, and press gently for 10 minutes to remove excess water. Toss the cubes in a bowl with the cornstarch and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook, turning every 2 minutes or so, for 8 to 10 minutes, until golden on most sides. Transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, the scallion whites, and the garlic to the skillet and stir for 30 seconds. Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, and the remaining salt and cook, stirring and mashing the tomatoes with a spatula, for 6 to 8 minutes, until they collapse into a chunky sauce.

Stir in the soy sauce, sugar, and 1/2 cup water and simmer for 2 minutes. Return the tofu to the pan and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, spooning the sauce over the cubes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat them.
Season with black pepper, scatter the scallion greens and cilantro over the top, and serve over the rice.

title: Egyptian-Style Koshari: Lentils, Rice and Pasta with Spiced Tomato Sauce
description: Egypt's well-loved street-food bowl: lentils, rice, and small pasta topped with a cumin and vinegar tomato sauce, chickpeas, and crisp fried onions. Filling, vegan, and about $1.10 a serving.
notes: The crispy onions are the soul of koshari, so take them all the way to deep brown; pale onions turn soft once they cool. Strain and save the onion oil, because it flavors the rice, pasta, and sauce. Elbow macaroni or broken spaghetti can replace the ditalini; gluten-free pasta makes the whole dish gluten-free. Stored separately, the rice and lentils, pasta, and sauce keep for 4 days in the refrigerator, and the sauce freezes for 3 months. Keep the onions in a loosely covered container at room temperature for up to 2 days and re-crisp them in a 350°F oven for 5 minutes. Cool cooked rice quickly and refrigerate everything within 2 hours; reheat until steaming hot (165°F).

ingredients.name: yellow onions (2 halved and very thinly sliced, 1 finely chopped)
kosher salt, divided, plus more for the pasta water
brown or green lentils (200 g), rinsed
long grain white rice (190 g), rinsed

instructions: Toss the sliced onions with the cornstarch and a pinch of the salt. Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat and fry the onions in two batches, stirring often, for 8 to 12 minutes per batch, until deep golden brown. Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto paper towels and sprinkle with salt. Pour the oil into a heatproof cup and save it.
Meanwhile, combine the lentils with 4 cups water in a medium saucepan, bring to a boil, and simmer for 15 minutes, until just tender but still firm. Drain.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the onion oil in the same saucepan over medium heat. Add the rice and 1/2 teaspoon of the cumin and stir for 1 minute. Add the drained lentils, 1 3/4 cups water, and 1 teaspoon of the salt, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 to 18 minutes. Let rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil and cook the ditalini for 8 to 9 minutes, until al dente. Drain and toss with 1 tablespoon of the onion oil.

For the sauce, heat 2 tablespoons of the onion oil in the skillet over medium heat. Cook the chopped onion for 5 to 6 minutes, until soft, then add 3 cloves of the garlic, 1 teaspoon of the cumin, the coriander, red pepper flakes, and cinnamon and stir for 30 seconds.

Add the crushed tomatoes, 1 tablespoon of the vinegar, the remaining 1 teaspoon salt, and the black pepper. Simmer, stirring now and then, for 15 to 20 minutes, until thick. Stir in the chickpeas for the last 5 minutes to warm them through.
For the garlic vinegar (daqqa), stir together the remaining 2 cloves garlic, 2 tablespoons vinegar, the last 1/2 teaspoon cumin, 1/4 cup water, and a pinch of salt.

To serve, spoon rice and lentils into each bowl, top with pasta, then the tomato sauce and chickpeas, and finish with a big handful of crispy onions. Pass the garlic vinegar at the table to drizzle over to taste.
